# truefoundry_provider_account (Resource)

Manages a TrueFoundry AI Gateway provider account and the models available through it. Applied as a `provider-account/<provider_type>` manifest via `PUT /api/svc/v1/apply`. Existing accounts can be imported by their FQN, e.g. `terraform import truefoundry_provider_account.example my-tenant:azure-openai:my-account`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# OpenAI: account-level API key.
resource "truefoundry_provider_account" "openai" {
  name    = "demo-openai"
  api_key = var.openai_api_key

  models = [
    {
      name        = "gpt-4o"
      model_id    = "gpt-4o"
      model_types = ["chat", "responses"]
    },
  ]
}

# Azure OpenAI: auth + endpoint on the account, deployments as models.
resource "truefoundry_provider_account" "azure_openai" {
  name           = "demo-azure-openai"
  provider_type  = "azure-openai"
  api_key        = var.azure_openai_api_key
  azure_endpoint = "https://demo.openai.azure.com"

  models = [
    {
      name             = "gpt-4o"
      model_id         = "gpt-4o-deployment" # Azure deployment name, not the base model
      api_version      = "2024-10-21"
      foundation_model = "gpt-4o-2024-11-20"
      deployment_type  = "datazone_eu"
      region           = "francecentral"
      model_types      = ["chat", "responses"]

      # Optional: pricing for gateway cost tracking.
      cost = {
        metric = "per_1000_tokens"
        input  = 0.0022
        output = 0.0088
      }
    },
  ]
}

# Azure AI Foundry: no account-level auth; endpoint + key per model deployment.
resource "truefoundry_provider_account" "azure_foundry" {
  name          = "demo-azure-foundry"
  provider_type = "azure-foundry"

  models = [
    {
      name           = "phi-4"
      model_id       = "phi-4-deployment"
      azure_endpoint = "https://phi-4.eastus.models.ai.azure.com"
      api_key        = "tfy-secret://my-tenant:my-secrets:phi-4-key" # per-model keys must be secret references
      api_version    = "2024-05-01-preview"
      model_types    = ["chat"]
    },
  ]
}

# AWS Bedrock: account-level region, access-key auth via secret references.
resource "truefoundry_provider_account" "bedrock" {
  name              = "demo-bedrock"
  provider_type     = "aws-bedrock"
  region            = "eu-central-1"
  access_key_id     = var.bedrock_access_key_id
  secret_access_key = var.bedrock_secret_access_key

  models = [
    {
      name        = "cohere-rerank-v3-5"
      model_id    = "cohere.rerank-v3-5:0"
      model_types = ["rerank"]
    },
  ]
}

# Virtual models: one gateway model name routed across real models.
resource "truefoundry_provider_account" "virtual" {
  name          = "demo-virtual"
  provider_type = "virtual-model"

  models = [
    {
      name        = "gpt-4o"
      model_types = ["chat", "responses"]
      routing = {
        type = "weight-based-routing"
        targets = [
          {
            target = "demo-azure-openai/gpt-4o"
            weight = 3
          },
          {
            target = "demo-openai/gpt-4o"
            weight = 1
          },
        ]
      }
    },
    {
      name        = "gpt-4o-failover"
      model_types = ["chat"]
      routing = {
        type = "priority-based-routing"
        targets = [
          {
            target                = "demo-azure-openai/gpt-4o"
            priority              = 0
            fallback_status_codes = ["429", "500"]
          },
          {
            target   = "demo-openai/gpt-4o"
            priority = 1
          },
        ]
      }
    },
  ]
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `models` (Attributes Set) Models exposed on the gateway through this provider account. Order is not significant. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--models))
- `name` (String) Name of the provider account (3-32 characters, or 3-64 for `virtual-model`; must start with a lowercase letter, end with a letter or digit, and contain only lowercase letters, digits and hyphens). Changing it replaces the account.

### Optional

- `access_key_id` (String, Sensitive) AWS access key ID (`aws-bedrock` only; alternative to `api_key`). Accepts a TrueFoundry secret reference (recommended).
- `api_key` (String, Sensitive) API key used by the gateway to authenticate against the model provider. Required for `openai` and `azure-openai`; for `aws-bedrock` it is an alternative to access keys; must be unset for `azure-foundry` (auth is per model there) and `virtual-model`. Accepts a TrueFoundry secret reference (recommended — keeps secret material out of the Terraform state); the control plane returns the value as stored, so drift is detected.
- `azure_endpoint` (String) Azure OpenAI Service endpoint URL, e.g. https://{resource-name}.openai.azure.com. Required for `azure-openai`.
- `base_url` (String) Optional custom base URL for the model provider API (`openai` only).
- `provider_type` (String) Model provider behind this account. One of: `openai`, `azure-openai`, `azure-foundry`, `virtual-model`, `aws-bedrock`.
- `region` (String) AWS region of the Bedrock account, e.g. eu-central-1. Required for `aws-bedrock`.
- `secret_access_key` (String, Sensitive) AWS secret access key (`aws-bedrock` only; required together with `access_key_id`). Accepts a TrueFoundry secret reference (recommended).

### Read-Only

- `fqn` (String) Fully qualified name of the provider account.
- `id` (String) Control plane ID of the provider account.

<a id="nestedatt--models"></a>
### Nested Schema for `models`

Required:

- `model_types` (Set of String) Model capabilities. One or more of: `chat`, `completion`, `embedding`, `realtime`, `rerank`, `audio_transcription`, `audio_translation`, `text_to_speech`, `moderation`, `image`, `responses`, `ocr`.
- `name` (String) Name identifying this model integration.

Optional:

- `api_key` (String) API key of the Azure AI Foundry deployment. Required for `azure-foundry` models, where auth is per model. Must be a TrueFoundry secret reference (`tfy-secret://...` or a `...:secret-store:...` FQN path) — raw keys are rejected: they would end up in the Terraform state, and per-model API keys are not treated as sensitive so that model diffs stay readable in plans.
- `api_version` (String) Azure API version, e.g. 2024-10-21. Required for `azure-openai` models, optional for `azure-foundry`.
- `authorized_subjects` (Set of String) Subjects allowed to access this model, e.g. `user:jane@example.com` or `team:my-team`. The control plane rejects `serviceaccount:` subjects here. Unset means account-level access.
- `azure_endpoint` (String) Azure AI Foundry endpoint URL, e.g. https://{deployment}.{region}.models.ai.azure.com. Required for `azure-foundry` models.
- `cost` (Attributes) Optional pricing of this model, used for gateway cost tracking. Token-based metrics (e.g. per_1000_tokens) use `input`/`output` rates; scalar metrics (e.g. per_1000_embedding_tokens, per_minute_of_audio) use `value`. Volume-based pricing tiers are not supported. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--models--cost))
- `deployment_type` (String) Azure OpenAI deployment type. One of: `standard`, `datazone_us`, `datazone_eu`, `global` (`azure-openai` only).
- `foundation_model` (String) Foundation model identifier behind the deployment, e.g. gpt-4o-2024-11-20 (`azure-openai` only).
- `model_id` (String) Provider model identifier or Azure deployment name, e.g. gpt-4o. Required for all provider types except `virtual-model`.
- `region` (String) Region of the deployment, e.g. francecentral (`azure-openai`) or a per-model AWS region override (`aws-bedrock`).
- `routing` (Attributes) Routing strategy of a virtual model across target models. Required for `virtual-model` models. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--models--routing))
- `slug` (String) Unique identifier of a virtual model, usable in place of `<group>/<model>` (`virtual-model` only).

<a id="nestedatt--models--cost"></a>
### Nested Schema for `models.cost`

Required:

- `metric` (String) Cost metric, e.g. per_1000_tokens or per_1000_embedding_tokens.

Optional:

- `cache_read` (Number) Cost per metric unit for cache reads.
- `cache_write` (Number) Cost per metric unit for cache writes.
- `input` (Number) Cost per metric unit for input tokens. Mutually exclusive with `value`.
- `output` (Number) Cost per metric unit for output tokens.
- `value` (Number) Cost per metric unit for scalar metrics. Mutually exclusive with `input`.


<a id="nestedatt--models--routing"></a>
### Nested Schema for `models.routing`

Required:

- `targets` (Attributes Set) Target models routed to. `weight` is required for weight-based routing, `priority` for priority-based routing. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--models--routing--targets))
- `type` (String) Routing strategy. One of: `weight-based-routing`, `priority-based-routing`.

<a id="nestedatt--models--routing--targets"></a>
### Nested Schema for `models.routing.targets`

Required:

- `target` (String) Target model as `<provider-account>/<model-name>`.

Optional:

- `fallback_candidate` (Boolean) Whether this target may serve as a fallback for other targets.
- `fallback_status_codes` (Set of String) Status codes for which the request falls back to other targets.
- `headers_override` (Attributes) Headers to remove from or set on the upstream request for this target. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--models--routing--targets--headers_override))
- `metadata_match` (Map of String) Metadata key-value pairs that must match incoming request metadata headers for this target to be considered.
- `priority` (Number) Priority of the target; 0 is highest (priority-based routing).
- `weight` (Number) Relative routing weight; higher values receive more traffic (weight-based routing).

<a id="nestedatt--models--routing--targets--headers_override"></a>
### Nested Schema for `models.routing.targets.headers_override`

Optional:

- `remove` (Set of String) Headers to remove from the upstream request.
- `set` (Map of String) Headers to add or overwrite on the upstream request.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Provider accounts are imported by their FQN: <tenant>:<provider-type>:<name>.
terraform import truefoundry_provider_account.azure_openai my-tenant:azure-openai:demo-azure-openai
```
